questions.q:
The number of units, which are used to express concentration of solutions from the following is _________.

(Mass percent, Mole, Mole fraction, Molarity, ppm, Molality.)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Both solute and solvent(solution) terms& are involved in the concentration term of solution. Mass percent, mole fraction, molarity, ppm, molality are used for measuring concentration terms. The number of moles is mass to molar mass ratio, it is not a concentration term for a solution.

questions.q:
An artificial cell is made by encapsulating (0.2 $\mathrm{M}$) glucose solution within a semipermeable membrane. The osmotic pressure developed when the artificial cell is placed within a (0.05 $\mathrm{M}$) solution of ($\mathrm{NaCl}$) at (300 $\mathrm{~K}$) is _______ ($\times$10^{-1}) bar. (nearest integer).
[Given : ($\mathrm{R}=$0.083 $\mathrm{~L} \mathrm{bar} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$)]
Assume complete dissociation of ($\mathrm{NaCl}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{NaCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-} \\ & 0.05 \mathrm{M} \quad 0.05 \mathrm{M} \quad 0.05 \mathrm{M} \\ & \text { Total } \mathrm{C}_1=0.05+0.05=0.1 \mathrm{M}(\mathrm{NaCl}) \\ & \mathrm{C}_2=0.2 \mathrm{M}(\text { glucose }) \\ & \pi=\left(\mathrm{C}_2-\mathrm{C}_1\right) \mathrm{RT} \\ & =(0.2-0.1) \times 0.083 \times 300 \\ & =2.49 \mathrm{bar} \\ & =24.9 \times 10^{-1} \text { bar }\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Molality of $0 . 8M{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ solution (density $1 . 06g{cm}^{- 3}$ ) is _______\times {10}^{- 3}m.

Round off your answer to the nearest integer.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$1000$ ml solution contains $0 . 8$mol of H2SO4

Mass of solution = $100{cm}^{3} \times 1 . 06\dfrac{g}{cm3} = 1060g$

Mass of solute (H2SO4) =$0 . 8 \times 98 = 78 . 4g$

Mass of solvent = $1060 - 78 . 4 = 981 . 6g$

$Molality = \dfrac{molesof{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}}{massofsolvent ( inkg )}$

$= \dfrac{0 . 8}{981 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}} = 0 . 815m$

= $815 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

questions.q: $2g$ of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute is disolved in $200g$ of two different solvents $A$ and $B$~whose ebullioscopic constants are in the ratio of $1: 8$. The elevation in boiling points of $A$ and $B$ are in the ratio $\dfrac{x}{y}  \left(x: y\right)$. The value of $y& is____(Nearest Integer)$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given :& $\dfrac{\left({K}_{b}\right)A}{\left({K}_{b}\right)B} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$∴ \dfrac{\left({ΔT}_{B}\right)A}{\left({ΔT}_{B}\right)B} = \dfrac{\left({K}_{b}\right)A \cdot m}{\left({K}_{b}\right)B \cdot m} = \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{x}{y}$

$∵ \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$∴ y = 8$& (nearest integer)

questions.q: A solution of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ is $31 . 4 % {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ by mass and has a density of $1 . 25g / mL$. The molarity of the ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ solution is $M$ (nearest integer) [Given molar mass of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4} = 98g{mol}^{- 1}$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given, Density= $1 . 25g / mL$,

Molar mass of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4} = 98g{mol}^{- 1}$

Molarity is defined as no. of moles of solute present in one litre of solution. Thus,

Molarity= $\dfrac{No . ofmolesofsolute}{VolumeofsolutioninL}$

No. of moles= mass/ molar mass

$M = \dfrac{n\text{solute}}{V} \times 1000$

$= \left(\dfrac{31 . 4}{98}\right)\left(\dfrac{100}{1 . 25}\right) \times 1000$

$= 4 . 005 \approx 4$

questions.q:
Lead storage battery contains $38 %$~by weight solution of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$. The van't Hoff factor is $2 . 67$ at this concentration. The temperature in Kelvin at which the solution in the battery will freeze is _____ (Nearest integer).

Given ${K}_{f} = 1 . 8Kkg{mol}^{- 1}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The depression in freezing point of the solution can be written as follows,

${ΔT}_{f} = i \cdot {K}_{f} \cdot m$

molality (m)~$= \dfrac{w / w %}{Molarmassofsolute} \times \dfrac{1000}{massofsolventingrams}$

$⇒ {ΔT}_{f} = 2 . 67 \times 1 . 8 \times \dfrac{38}{98} \times \dfrac{1000}{62}$

$⇒ {ΔT}_{f} = 30 . 05$

$∴$~Freezing point of solution at which battery freeze$= 243K$

questions.q: $0 . 004M{K}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ solution is isotonic with $0 . 01M$ glucose solution. Percentage dissociation of ${K}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ is _____ (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Osmotic pressure& $\pi = iCRT$

$i =$Van't Hoff Factor

$C =$Molarity

$R =$Same gas constant

$T =$Temperature

For isotonic solutions, osmotic pressure are equal, Hence, we have

$( 0 . 004 ) \times i = 0 . 01$

$⇒ i = \dfrac{0 . 01}{0 . 004}$

$= \dfrac{10}{4} = \dfrac{5}{2} = 1 + 2\alpha$

$2\alpha = 1 . 5$

$\alpha = 0 . 75$

$% \alpha = 75$

questions.q: Elevation in boiling point for $1 . 5$~molal solution of glucose in water is $4K$. The depression in freezing point for $4 . 5$~molal solution of glucose in water is $4K$. The ratio of molal elevation constant to molal depression constant  \left({K}_{b} / {K}_{f}\right)$ is$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Elevation in boiling point& $∆ {T}_{b} = {ik}_{b}{m}_{1}$

Depression in freezing point~$∆ {T}_{f} = {ik}_{f}{m}_{2}$

$4 = {ik}_{b} \left(1 . 5\right)$

$4 = {ik}_{f} \left(4 . 5\right)$

Dividing both:

$\dfrac{kb}{kf} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

Hence,& The ratio of molal elevation constant to molal depression constant is& 3:1

questions.q: $150g$ of acetic acid was contaminated with $10 . 2g$ ascorbic acid  \left({C}_{6}{H}_{8}{O}_{6}\right)$ to lower down its freezing point by \left(x \times {10}^{- 1}\right) ° C$. The value of $x$ is____ (Nearest integer). [Given ${K}_{f} = 3 . 9Kkg{mol}^{- 1}$; Molar mass of ascorbic acid $= 176g{mol}^{- 1}]$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given& $150gofsolvent{CH}_{3}COOH$

And as solute~$10 . 2g$~ascorbic acid $= \dfrac{10 . 2}{176} = 0 . 058$ moles

${ΔT}_{f} = \left(x \times {10}^{- 1}\right) ° C$

${ΔT}_{f} = {k}_{f} \cdot$ molality

$= 3 . 9 \times \dfrac{0 . 058}{150} \times 1000$

$= 1 . 5 ° C$

$= 15 \times {10}^{- 1} ° C$

So, value of x=15.

questions.q: If the degree of dissociation of aqueous solution of weak monobasic acid is determined to be $0 . 3$, then the observed freezing point will be _____ $%$ higher than the expected/theoretical freezing point. (Nearest integer).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\mathop{HA}_{1 - \alpha} ⇋ \mathop{H +}_{α} + \mathop{A -}_{α}$

Van't Hoff factor,~$i = 1 + \alpha \left(n - 1\right)$

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } $= 1 + 0 . 3 \left(2 - 1\right)$

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ & & & & & & & $= 1 + 0 . 3$

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ & & & & & & & & $= 1 . 3$

$∆ {T}_{f}$ without considering dissociation $= {k}_{f} \times$~molality

$∆ {T}_{f}$ without considering dissociation $= {ik}_{f} \times$molality

$= {ΔT}_f^{'}$

${ΔT}_f^{'} - {ΔT}_{f} = 0 . 3$~(${k}_{f} \times$molality)

$\dfrac{{ΔT}_f^{1} - {ΔT}_{f}}{\Delta Tf} = \dfrac{0 . 3\left({k}_{f} \times molality\right)}{{k}_{f} \times molality} =0 . 3$

$%$ value $= 30$

questions.q: A solution containing $2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}kg$ of a solute dissolved in $75 \times {10}^{- 3}kg$ of water boils at $373 . 535K$. The molar mass of the solute is ${mol}^{- 1} \cdot$ [nearest integer] (Given : ${K}_{b}\left({H}_{2}O\right) = 0 . 52Kkg{mol}^{- 1}$ and boiling point of water $= 373 . 15K$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${ΔT}_{b} = {iK}_{b}m$

${ΔT}_{b} = Elevationofboilingpoint{K}_{b} = molalboilingpointelevationconstantm = molalityi = van ' thofffactor$

$m = \dfrac{2 . 5}{M} \times \dfrac{1000}{75}$

$∆ {T}_{b} = {T}_{b} - {T}_b^{o}{T}_{b} = Boilingpointofthesolution{T}_b^{o} = Boilingpointofthesolvent ∆ {T}_{b} = 373 . 535 - 373 . 15 = 0 . 385K$

${ΔT}_{b} = {iK}_{b}m$

$0 . 385 = 1 \times 0 . 52 \times \dfrac{2 . 5 \times 1000}{M \times 75}$

The molar mass of the solute,$M = 45g / ml$.
